question: For every account, count ledger entries posted on or before March 31, 2025, and sum their signed amounts. Include accounts without qualifying entries with count zero and net change zero. Return account_number, entry_count, and net_change rounded to two decimals, ordered by account_number.
sql:
SELECT a.account_number,
       COUNT(le.entry_id) AS entry_count,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN le.entry_type = 'credit' THEN le.amount WHEN le.entry_type = 'debit' THEN -le.amount ELSE 0 END), 0), 2) AS net_change
FROM accounts a
LEFT JOIN ledger_entries le 
  ON a.account_id = le.account_id
 AND le.posted_at <= '2025-03-31'
GROUP BY a.account_number
ORDER BY a.account_number;
reference_sql:
SELECT a.account_number,
       COUNT(l.entry_id) AS entry_count,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0), 2) AS net_change
FROM ledger_entries l
RIGHT JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id = l.account_id
AND l.posted_at < '2025-04-01'
GROUP BY a.account_id,
         a.account_number
ORDER BY a.account_number;
classification_explanation: The request can be answered using the schema: 'accounts' provides account_number, and 'ledger_entries' provides posted_at and amount. The request can be fulfilled by joining these tables and performing aggregation, while including accounts with no qualifying entries by using an outer join. Rounding and ordering are possible with available data.

question: For every customer, report the number of tickets of any status and the number of those tickets with no assigned agent. Include customers without tickets with both counts zero. Return customer_id, customer_name, ticket_count, and unassigned_ticket_count, sorted by customer_id ascending.
sql:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.name AS customer_name, COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS ticket_count, SUM(CASE WHEN t.assigned_agent_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unassigned_ticket_count
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN tickets t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name
ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;
reference_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.name AS customer_name,
       COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS ticket_count,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN t.ticket_id IS NOT NULL
                    AND t.assigned_agent_id IS NULL THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END) AS unassigned_ticket_count
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN tickets AS t ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id,
         c.name
ORDER BY c.customer_id;
classification_explanation: This is a valid read-only database request. The user asks for customer information along with ticket counts, including both total tickets and tickets without an assigned agent, ensuring customers with no tickets are included with zero counts. All necessary data can be found in the customers and tickets tables, and the requested columns are available in the schema.

question: For each team, identify all agents tied for the largest number of assigned unresolved tickets, meaning status open or pending. Exclude teams where every agent has zero assigned unresolved tickets. Count workload by the agent's team, and ignore unassigned tickets. Return team_id, team_name, agent_id, agent_name, and unresolved_ticket_count, sorted by team_id ascending, then agent_id ascending.
sql:
WITH unresolved_tickets AS (
  SELECT
    assigned_agent_id AS agent_id,
    team_id,
    COUNT(*) AS unresolved_ticket_count
  FROM tickets
  WHERE assigned_agent_id IS NOT NULL
    AND status IN ('open', 'pending')
  GROUP BY assigned_agent_id, team_id
),
max_counts AS (
  SELECT
    team_id,
    MAX(unresolved_ticket_count) AS max_unresolved
  FROM unresolved_tickets
  GROUP BY team_id
),
having_max AS (
  SELECT
    ut.team_id,
    ut.agent_id,
    ut.unresolved_ticket_count
  FROM unresolved_tickets ut
  INNER JOIN max_counts mc
    ON ut.team_id = mc.team_id AND ut.unresolved_ticket_count = mc.max_unresolved
  WHERE ut.unresolved_ticket_count > 0
)
SELECT
  t.team_id,
  t.name AS team_name,
  a.agent_id,
  a.name AS agent_name,
  hm.unresolved_ticket_count
FROM having_max hm
JOIN teams t ON hm.team_id = t.team_id
JOIN agents a ON hm.agent_id = a.agent_id
ORDER BY t.team_id ASC, a.agent_id ASC
LIMIT 100;
reference_sql:
WITH workloads AS
    (SELECT a.team_id,
            a.agent_id,
            a.name AS agent_name,
            COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS unresolved_ticket_count
     FROM agents AS a
     LEFT JOIN tickets AS t ON t.assigned_agent_id = a.agent_id
     AND t.status IN ('open',
                      'pending')
     GROUP BY a.team_id,
              a.agent_id,
              a.name),
     ranked AS
    (SELECT *,
            DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY team_id
                               ORDER BY unresolved_ticket_count DESC) AS POSITION
     FROM workloads)
SELECT tm.team_id,
       tm.name AS team_name,
       r.agent_id,
       r.agent_name,
       r.unresolved_ticket_count
FROM ranked AS r
INNER JOIN teams AS tm ON tm.team_id = r.team_id
WHERE r.position = 1
    AND r.unresolved_ticket_count > 0
ORDER BY tm.team_id,
         r.agent_id;
classification_explanation: The request is to find, for each team, the agents who have the most assigned unresolved tickets (those tickets assigned to an agent and with status 'open' or 'pending'), where unresolved tickets are counted only within the agent's team, and teams where all agents have zero unresolved tickets are excluded. It requires joins between teams, agents, and tickets, groupings, counts, and conditions as specified, all of which are possible with the provided schema.

question: Which checked_out bookings still have a positive outstanding balance? Balance equals nights excluding checkout day times booked_nightly_rate, minus all signed payments for that booking; treat no payments as zero. Return booking_id, guest_name, room_number, and outstanding_balance rounded to two decimal places, sorted by booking_id ascending. Test positivity before rounding.
sql:
SELECT 
  b.booking_id,
  g.name AS guest_name,
  r.room_number,
  ROUND(
    (
      (julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in)) - 1
    ) * b.booked_nightly_rate - IFNULL(p.total_paid, 0),
    2
  ) AS outstanding_balance
FROM bookings b
JOIN guests g ON b.guest_id = g.guest_id
JOIN rooms r ON b.room_id = r.room_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT booking_id, SUM(amount) AS total_paid
  FROM payments
  GROUP BY booking_id
) p ON b.booking_id = p.booking_id
WHERE b.status = 'checked_out'
  AND ((
      ((julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in)) - 1) * b.booked_nightly_rate - IFNULL(p.total_paid, 0)
    ) > 0)
ORDER BY b.booking_id ASC
LIMIT 100;
reference_sql:
SELECT b.booking_id,
       g.name AS guest_name,
       r.room_number,
       ROUND((julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in)) * b.booked_nightly_rate - COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0), 2) AS outstanding_balance
FROM bookings AS b
INNER JOIN guests AS g ON g.guest_id = b.guest_id
INNER JOIN rooms AS r ON r.room_id = b.room_id
LEFT JOIN payments AS p ON p.booking_id = b.booking_id
WHERE b.status = 'checked_out'
GROUP BY b.booking_id,
         g.name,
         r.room_number,
         b.check_in,
         b.check_out,
         b.booked_nightly_rate
HAVING (julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in)) * b.booked_nightly_rate - COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0) > 0
ORDER BY b.booking_id;
classification_explanation: The request asks for bookings with the status 'checked_out' and a positive outstanding balance, calculated based on database fields. All required data is available in the schema: nights (from check_in/check_out), booked_nightly_rate (from bookings), payments, and guest/room details. This falls within read-only, answerable queries.

question: For each part with at least one completed work order, show the total completed quantity and the number of distinct direct component parts in its bill of materials. The completed quantity must count each work order once; a part without direct components has a component count of zero. Return part_id, name, completed_quantity, component_count, ordered by part_id ascending.
sql:
SELECT 
    p.id AS part_id,
    p.name,
    COALESCE(SUM(wo.quantity), 0) AS completed_quantity,
    COUNT(DISTINCT b.component_part_id) AS component_count
FROM parts p
JOIN work_orders wo ON p.id = wo.part_id
LEFT JOIN bom b ON p.id = b.parent_part_id
WHERE wo.completed_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.id, p.name
ORDER BY p.id ASC
LIMIT 100;
reference_sql:
WITH completed AS
    (SELECT part_id,
            SUM(quantity) AS completed_quantity
     FROM work_orders
     WHERE status = 'completed'
     GROUP BY part_id),
     components AS
    (SELECT parent_part_id,
            COUNT(*) AS component_count
     FROM bom
     GROUP BY parent_part_id)
SELECT p.id AS part_id,
       p.name,
       c.completed_quantity,
       COALESCE(b.component_count, 0) AS component_count
FROM completed AS c
JOIN parts AS p ON p.id = c.part_id
LEFT JOIN components AS b ON b.parent_part_id = p.id
ORDER BY p.id;
classification_explanation: The request asks for, per part with at least one completed work order, the total completed quantity (sum of quantities from completed work orders), and the number of distinct direct component parts in its bill of materials. All relevant data is available in the 'parts', 'work_orders', and 'bom' tables, and the columns required exist. The request is fully answerable with the given schema.

question: Find the product or products with the highest completed-order revenue within each category, including ties. Include all catalog products in the comparison with zero revenue when unsold. Return category, product ID, name, and revenue rounded to two decimals; sort category then product ID. Use historical item prices.
sql:
WITH CompletedOrderRevenue AS (
  SELECT 
    p.category,
    p.id AS product_id,
    p.name,
    COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) AS revenue
  FROM products p
  LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.id = oi.product_id
  LEFT JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.id AND o.status = 'completed'
  GROUP BY p.category, p.id, p.name
),
MaxRevenuePerCategory AS (
  SELECT category, MAX(revenue) AS max_revenue
  FROM CompletedOrderRevenue
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT 
  c.category,
  c.product_id,
  c.name,
  ROUND(c.revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM CompletedOrderRevenue c
JOIN MaxRevenuePerCategory m ON c.category = m.category AND c.revenue = m.max_revenue
ORDER BY c.category, c.product_id;
reference_sql:
WITH totals AS
    (SELECT p.id,
            p.name,
            p.category,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE
                             WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN i.quantity * i.unit_price
                             ELSE 0
                         END), 0) AS revenue
     FROM products p
     LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.id
     LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id
     GROUP BY p.id,
              p.name,
              p.category),
     ranked AS
    (SELECT *,
            DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category
                               ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS POSITION
     FROM totals)
SELECT category,
       id,
       name,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE POSITION = 1
ORDER BY category,
         id;
classification_explanation: The request is fully answerable using the provided schema. It involves aggregating revenue for products based on completed orders and product prices stored historically in order_items. The query can include all products, even those with zero sales, and return the requested fields with the required sorting and rounding. This is a valid read-only database question.

question: Which students have completed every required course in their own major in any term? Exclude majors with no required courses. Return student ID and name, sorted by ID.
sql:
WITH RequiredCourses AS (
  SELECT major, id AS course_id
  FROM courses
  WHERE is_required = 1
),
MajorsWithRequiredCourses AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT major
  FROM courses
  WHERE is_required = 1
),
StudentRequiredCourses AS (
  SELECT s.id AS student_id, s.major, rc.course_id
  FROM students s
  JOIN RequiredCourses rc ON s.major = rc.major
),
CompletedInTerm AS (
  SELECT e.student_id, e.term, e.course_id
  FROM enrollments e
  WHERE e.status = 'completed'
),
StudentTermCompletion AS (
  SELECT ctr.student_id, ctr.term
  FROM CompletedInTerm ctr
  JOIN StudentRequiredCourses src ON ctr.student_id = src.student_id AND ctr.course_id = src.course_id
  GROUP BY ctr.student_id, ctr.term
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ctr.course_id) = (
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses c WHERE c.major = src.major AND c.is_required = 1
  )
)
SELECT DISTINCT s.id, s.name
FROM students s
JOIN MajorsWithRequiredCourses m ON s.major = m.major
JOIN StudentTermCompletion stc ON s.id = stc.student_id
ORDER BY s.id;
reference_sql:
SELECT s.id,
       s.name
FROM students s
WHERE EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM courses c
         WHERE c.major = s.major
             AND c.is_required = 1)
    AND NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM courses c
         WHERE c.major = s.major
             AND c.is_required = 1
             AND NOT EXISTS
                 (SELECT 1
                  FROM enrollments e
                  WHERE e.student_id = s.id
                      AND e.course_id = c.id
                      AND e.status = 'completed'))
ORDER BY s.id;
classification_explanation: This is a valid read-only database question asking for students who have completed every required course in their own major, with results including student ID and name sorted by ID. The schema provides courses, enrollments, and students tables that contain the necessary data to answer this question.

question: Produce a reconciliation list containing every appointment and every payment, matching payments to appointments when possible. Keep one row per matched payment, appointments with no payment, and unallocated payments. Return appointment_id, payment_id, and amount; leave missing values NULL. Order by appointment_id with NULLs last, then payment_id.

WITH unmatched_payments AS (
  SELECT p.payment_id, p.amount
  FROM payments p
  LEFT JOIN appointments a ON p.appointment_id = a.appointment_id
  WHERE a.appointment_id IS NULL
), matched AS (
  SELECT a.appointment_id, p.payment_id, p.amount
  FROM appointments a
  LEFT JOIN payments p ON a.appointment_id = p.appointment_id
)
SELECT appointment_id, payment_id, amount
FROM matched
UNION ALL
SELECT NULL AS appointment_id, payment_id, amount
FROM unmatched_payments
ORDER BY (appointment_id IS NULL), appointment_id, payment_id;

       p.payment_id,
       p.amount
FROM appointments a
FULL OUTER JOIN payments p ON p.appointment_id = a.appointment_id
ORDER BY a.appointment_id IS NULL,
                             a.appointment_id,
                             p.payment_id;

question: Reconcile all local accounts with all imported statements dated March 31, 2025, retaining unmatched records on either side. Return account_number, book_balance, statement_balance, and the rounded book balance minus the rounded statement balance as difference. Book balance uses opening_balance plus postings through March 31. Round monetary outputs to two decimals; use NULL for a missing book balance, a missing or unknown statement balance, and any difference involving NULL. Order by account_number ascending.
sql:
WITH postings AS (
  SELECT
    le.account_id,
    ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(le.amount), 0) + a.opening_balance, 2) AS book_balance
  FROM ledger_entries le
  JOIN accounts a ON le.account_id = a.account_id
  WHERE DATE(le.posted_at) <= '2025-03-31'
  GROUP BY le.account_id
), book_balances AS (
  SELECT
    a.account_number,
    p.book_balance
  FROM accounts a
  LEFT JOIN postings p ON a.account_id = p.account_id
  WHERE a.kind = 'local'
), stmt AS (
  SELECT
    account_number,
    ROUND(ending_balance, 2) AS statement_balance
  FROM statements
  WHERE statement_date = '2025-03-31'
), combined AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(b.account_number, s.account_number) AS account_number,
    b.book_balance,
    s.statement_balance
  FROM book_balances b
  LEFT JOIN stmt s ON b.account_number = s.account_number
  UNION
  SELECT
    COALESCE(b.account_number, s.account_number) AS account_number,
    b.book_balance,
    s.statement_balance
  FROM stmt s
  LEFT JOIN book_balances b ON s.account_number = b.account_number
)
SELECT
  account_number,
  book_balance,
  statement_balance,
  CASE
    WHEN book_balance IS NULL OR statement_balance IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE ROUND(book_balance, 2) - ROUND(statement_balance, 2)
  END AS difference
FROM combined
ORDER BY account_number ASC
LIMIT 100;
reference_sql:
WITH book AS
    (SELECT a.account_number,
            ROUND(a.opening_balance + COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0), 2) AS book_balance
     FROM accounts a
     LEFT JOIN ledger_entries l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
     AND l.posted_at < '2025-04-01'
     GROUP BY a.account_id,
              a.account_number,
              a.opening_balance),
     imported AS
    (SELECT account_number,
            ending_balance
     FROM statements
     WHERE statement_date = '2025-03-31')
SELECT COALESCE(b.account_number, s.account_number) AS account_number,
       b.book_balance,
       ROUND(s.ending_balance, 2) AS statement_balance,
       ROUND(b.book_balance - ROUND(s.ending_balance, 2), 2) AS difference
FROM book b
FULL OUTER JOIN imported s ON s.account_number = b.account_number
ORDER BY account_number;
classification_explanation: The user's request is an answerable read-only database query involving the provided schema. It asks to reconcile accounts with statements by comparing balances as of March 31, 2025, which can be constructed from the accounts opening_balance and ledger_entries up to that date, along with statements matching the date. All required tables (accounts, ledger_entries, statements) and columns are available to fulfill the query.

question: Which checked_out bookings still have a positive outstanding balance? Balance equals nights excluding checkout day times booked_nightly_rate, minus all signed payments for that booking; treat no payments as zero. WITH booking_nights AS (
  SELECT
    booking_id,
    guest_id,
    room_id,
    status,
    booked_nightly_rate,
    CAST((julianday(check_out) - julianday(check_in)) - 1 AS INTEGER) AS nights,

  WHERE status = 'checked_out'
),
payments_sum AS (
  SELECT
    booking_id,
    COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) AS total_paid
  FROM payments
  GROUP BY booking_id
),
balances AS (

question: Within each room type, find every room tied for the highest total booking value from checked_out stays. Use historical booked_nightly_rate times nights excluding checkout days, and assign zero to rooms without checked_out stays; if every room in a type has zero, return all of them. Return room_type, room_number, and completed_booking_value rounded to two decimal places. Rank using unrounded totals and sort by room_type alphabetically, then room_number ascending.
sql:
WITH CompletedBookings AS (
    SELECT
        r.room_id,
        r.room_number,
        r.room_type,
        COALESCE(SUM((julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in) - 1) * b.booked_nightly_rate), 0) AS total_value
    FROM rooms r
    LEFT JOIN bookings b ON r.room_id = b.room_id AND b.status = 'checked_out'
    GROUP BY r.room_id
),
RoomTypeMax AS (
    SELECT
        room_type,
        MAX(total_value) AS max_value
    FROM CompletedBookings
    GROUP BY room_type
),
RoomTypeAllZero AS (
    SELECT
        room_type
    FROM RoomTypeMax
    WHERE max_value = 0
)
SELECT
    c.room_type,
    c.room_number,
    ROUND(c.total_value, 2) AS completed_booking_value
FROM CompletedBookings c
JOIN RoomTypeMax m ON c.room_type = m.room_type
WHERE
    (c.total_value = m.max_value AND m.max_value > 0) OR
    (c.room_type IN (SELECT room_type FROM RoomTypeAllZero))
ORDER BY
    c.room_type ASC,
    c.room_number ASC;

WITH room_values AS
    (SELECT r.room_id,
            r.room_number,
            r.room_type,
            COALESCE(SUM((julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in)) * b.booked_nightly_rate), 0) AS booking_value
     FROM rooms AS r
     LEFT JOIN bookings AS b ON b.room_id = r.room_id
     AND b.status = 'checked_out'
     GROUP BY r.room_id,
              r.room_number,
              r.room_type),
     ranked AS
    (SELECT *,
            DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY room_type
                               ORDER BY booking_value DESC) AS POSITION
     FROM room_values)
SELECT room_type,
       room_number,
       ROUND(booking_value, 2) AS completed_booking_value
FROM ranked
WHERE POSITION = 1
ORDER BY room_type,
         room_number;

question: Show every pair of adjacent stop positions on the same route, where the destination sequence is exactly one greater than the origin sequence.   rs1.stop_sequence AS origin_sequence,
  rs1.stop_id AS origin_stop,
  rs2.stop_id AS destination_stop,
  rs2.travel_minutes_from_previous AS segment_minutes
FROM route_stops rs1

ORDER BY rs1.route_id, rs1.stop_sequence

question: For every visitor, total their purchase-event revenue, using zero for visitors without purchases or sessions. Rank visitors by unrounded revenue ascending with equal revenues sharing the first position occupied by that tie group, and calculate percentile_fraction as (rank minus one) divided by (number of visitors minus one); use zero if there is only one visitor. Return visitor_id, country, purchase_revenue rounded to two decimals, percentile_fraction rounded to four decimals, ordered by unrounded purchase revenue and then visitor_id ascending.
sql:
WITH visitor_revenue AS (
    SELECT v.id AS visitor_id, v.country, COALESCE(SUM(e.revenue), 0) AS purchase_revenue
    FROM visitors v
    LEFT JOIN sessions s ON s.visitor_id = v.id
    LEFT JOIN events e ON e.session_id = s.id AND e.event_type = 'purchase'
    GROUP BY v.id, v.country
),
ranks AS (
    SELECT
        visitor_id,
        country,
        purchase_revenue,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY purchase_revenue ASC) AS dense_rank,
        COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_visitors
    FROM visitor_revenue
),
tie_counts AS (
    SELECT
        purchase_revenue,
        COUNT(*) AS tie_count
    FROM ranks
    GROUP BY purchase_revenue
),
rank_with_ties AS (
    SELECT
        r.visitor_id,
        r.country,
        r.purchase_revenue,
        r.dense_rank,
        r.total_visitors,
        tc.tie_count
    FROM ranks r
    JOIN tie_counts tc ON r.purchase_revenue = tc.purchase_revenue
),
percentiles AS (
    SELECT
        visitor_id,
        country,
        purchase_revenue,
        dense_rank,
        total_visitors,
        tie_count,
        CASE
            WHEN total_visitors = 1 THEN 0
            ELSE ((dense_rank - 1) + (tie_count - 1) * 0.5) / (total_visitors - 1)
        END AS percentile_fraction
    FROM rank_with_ties
)
SELECT
    visitor_id,
    country,
    ROUND(purchase_revenue, 2) AS purchase_revenue,
    ROUND(percentile_fraction, 4) AS percentile_fraction
FROM percentiles
ORDER BY purchase_revenue, visitor_id ASC;

question: Find open accounts whose current balance is strictly below the average current balance of open accounts of the same kind. Current balance includes opening_balance and all postings; include accounts with no entries in the comparison. Compare unrounded balances. Return account_number, kind, and current_balance rounded to two decimals, ordered by account_number.

WITH current_balances AS (  
    SELECT  
        a.account_number,  
        a.kind,  
        ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN le.entry_type = 'credit' THEN le.amount ELSE -le.amount END), 0) + a.opening_balance, 2) AS current_balance  
    FROM accounts a  
    LEFT JOIN ledger_entries le ON a.account_id = le.account_id  
    WHERE a.status = 'open'  
    GROUP BY a.account_id  
), average_balances AS (  
    SELECT

    FROM current_balances  
    GROUP BY kind  
)  
SELECT  
    cb.account_number,  
    cb.kind,  
    cb.current_balance  
FROM current_balances cb  
JOIN average_balances ab ON cb.kind = ab.kind  
WHERE cb.current_balance < ab.avg_current_balance

question: Calculate the leaf-material requirements for building three Desk lamps (part_id 1). A leaf material is a descendant with no components of its own. Multiply quantities along each path, add quantities when a leaf appears along multiple paths, and price the resulting quantity at the leaf part's unit_cost. Return leaf_part_id, name, required_quantity, material_cost rounded to two decimal places, ordered by leaf_part_id ascending.
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
  path(leaf, qty, depth) AS (
    -- start from root's direct components (root_id = 1)
    SELECT b.component_part_id AS leaf,
           b.quantity AS qty,
           1 AS depth
    FROM bom b
    WHERE b.parent_part_id = 1

    UNION ALL
    -- extend paths with a depth guard to guarantee termination
    SELECT b.component_part_id AS leaf,
           p.qty * b.quantity AS qty,
           p.depth + 1 AS depth
    FROM path p
    JOIN bom b ON b.parent_part_id = p.leaf
    WHERE p.depth + 1 <= 1000
  )
SELECT
  path.leaf AS leaf_part_id,
  p_leaf.name,
  SUM(path.qty) AS required_quantity,
  ROUND(SUM(path.qty) * p_leaf.unit_cost, 2) AS material_cost
FROM path
JOIN parts p_leaf ON p_leaf.id = path.leaf
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bom b3 WHERE b3.parent_part_id = path.leaf)
GROUP BY path.leaf, p_leaf.name, p_leaf.unit_cost
ORDER BY path.leaf ASC
LIMIT 1000;

     UNION ALL SELECT b.component_part_id,
                      r.required_quantity * b.quantity
     FROM requirements AS r
     JOIN bom AS b ON b.parent_part_id = r.part_id)
SELECT p.id AS leaf_part_id,
       p.name,
       SUM(r.required_quantity) AS required_quantity,
       ROUND(SUM(r.required_quantity) * p.unit_cost, 2) AS material_cost
FROM requirements AS r

question: For each nonmissing reading with a matching regional tariff, show the tariff effective on that reading's UTC calendar date. The valid_from date is inclusive, valid_to is exclusive, and NULL valid_to has no upper limit. Return reading_id, meter_id, reading_date formatted YYYY-MM-DD, price_per_kwh, ordered by reading_id ascending.
sql:
WITH active AS (
  SELECT r.id AS reading_id,
         r.meter_id,
         strftime('%Y-%m-%d', r.reading_at, 'utc') AS reading_date,
         t.price_per_kwh,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY r.id
           ORDER BY date(t.valid_from) DESC, t.id DESC
         ) AS rn
  FROM readings r
  JOIN meters m ON r.meter_id = m.id
  JOIN sites s ON m.site_id = s.id
  JOIN tariffs t ON t.region = s.region
  WHERE r.reading_kwh IS NOT NULL
    AND date(r.reading_at, 'utc') >= date(t.valid_from)
    AND (t.valid_to IS NULL OR date(r.reading_at, 'utc') < date(t.valid_to))
)
SELECT reading_id,
       meter_id,
       reading_date,
       price_per_kwh
FROM active
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY reading_id ASC
LIMIT 1000

JOIN sites AS s ON s.id = m.site_id

question: For each registered participant group, compute the percentage of mandatory question-participant combinations that have a non-NULL score. The denominator is all registered participants in the group times the total number of mandatory questions; skips and missing responses are incomplete. Return group_name (Unassigned for NULL) and completion_percent rounded to two decimals, ordered by group_name. Use NULL if there are no mandatory questions.
sql:
WITH mandatory AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM questions WHERE required = 1
),
groups AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(p.group_name, 'Unassigned') AS group_name, COUNT(*) AS participant_count
  FROM participants p
  GROUP BY COALESCE(p.group_name, 'Unassigned')
),
numerator AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(p.group_name, 'Unassigned') AS group_name,
         COUNT(DISTINCT (r.participant_id || ':' || r.question_id)) AS numerator
  FROM responses r
  JOIN questions q ON r.question_id = q.id
  JOIN participants p ON r.participant_id = p.id
  WHERE q.required = 1 AND r.score IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY COALESCE(p.group_name, 'Unassigned')
)
SELECT g.group_name,
       CASE WHEN m.cnt = 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE ROUND((COALESCE(n.numerator, 0) * 1.0) / (g.participant_count * m.cnt), 2)
       END AS completion_percent
FROM groups g
CROSS JOIN mandatory m
LEFT JOIN numerator n ON n.group_name = g.group_name
ORDER BY g.group_name
LIMIT 1000;
reference_sql:
SELECT COALESCE(p.group_name, 'Unassigned') AS group_name,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(
                             (SELECT COUNT(*)
                              FROM responses r
                              JOIN questions q ON q.id = r.question_id
                              WHERE r.participant_id = p.id
                                  AND q.required = 1
                                  AND r.score IS NOT NULL)) / NULLIF(COUNT(*) *
                                                                         (SELECT COUNT(*)
                                                                          FROM questions
                                                                          WHERE required = 1), 0), 2) AS completion_percent
FROM participants p
GROUP BY COALESCE(p.group_name, 'Unassigned')
ORDER BY group_name;

question: For every project, return project_id, name, known_cost, and unpriced_hours, in that order. Include all task statuses and dates. Known cost is the sum of hours times billed_rate for entries with a non-NULL rate; unpriced hours are hours with a NULL rate. Use zero for missing totals and projects with no work, round both totals to two decimals, and sort by project_id ascending.
sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS project_id,
  p.name,
  COALESCE(ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN te.billed_rate IS NOT NULL THEN te.hours * te.billed_rate ELSE 0 END), 2), 0) AS known_cost,
  COALESCE(ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN te.billed_rate IS NULL THEN te.hours ELSE 0 END), 2), 0) AS unpriced_hours,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(t.id) > 0 THEN
    COALESCE(GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT t.status), '') || ';' || COALESCE(GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT t.due_date), '')
  ELSE '' END AS statuses_and_dates
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN tasks t ON t.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN time_entries te ON te.task_id = t.id
GROUP BY p.id, p.name
ORDER BY p.id ASC;

       p.name,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(e.hours * e.billed_rate), 0), 2) AS known_cost,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE
                              WHEN e.billed_rate IS NULL THEN e.hours
                              ELSE 0
                          END), 0), 2) AS unpriced_hours
FROM projects AS p
LEFT JOIN tasks AS t ON t.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN time_entries AS e ON e.task_id = t.id
GROUP BY p.id,

question: For every project, return project_id, task_count, dependency_edge_count, and total_hours, in that order. Count each task once, count each direct dependency edge once for the project owning its dependent task, and sum each time entry once. Include all statuses and dates, preserve projects without tasks with zero totals, round hours to two decimals, and sort by project_id ascending.
sql:
WITH t_counts AS (
    SELECT t.project_id AS project_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.id) AS task_count
    FROM tasks t
    GROUP BY t.project_id
), dep_counts AS (
    SELECT t.project_id AS project_id, COUNT(dt.id) AS dependency_edge_count
    FROM tasks t
    LEFT JOIN dependencies d ON d.task_id = t.id
    LEFT JOIN tasks dt ON dt.id = d.depends_on AND dt.project_id = t.project_id
    GROUP BY t.project_id
), hours_sum AS (
    SELECT t.project_id AS project_id, SUM(COALESCE(te.hours, 0)) AS total_hours
    FROM tasks t
    LEFT JOIN time_entries te ON te.task_id = t.id
    GROUP BY t.project_id
)
SELECT p.id AS project_id,
       COALESCE(tc.task_count, 0) AS task_count,
       COALESCE(dc.dependency_edge_count, 0) AS dependency_edge_count,
       ROUND(COALESCE(hs.total_hours, 0), 2) AS total_hours
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN t_counts tc ON tc.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN dep_counts dc ON dc.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN hours_sum hs ON hs.project_id = p.id
ORDER BY p.id ASC
LIMIT 100;
reference_sql:
WITH task_totals AS
    (SELECT project_id,
            COUNT(*) AS task_count
     FROM tasks
     GROUP BY project_id),
     dependency_totals AS
    (SELECT t.project_id,
            COUNT(*) AS dependency_edge_count
     FROM tasks AS t
     JOIN dependencies AS d ON d.task_id = t.id
     GROUP BY t.project_id),
     time_totals AS
    (SELECT t.project_id,
            SUM(e.hours) AS total_hours
     FROM tasks AS t
     JOIN time_entries AS e ON e.task_id = t.id
     GROUP BY t.project_id)
SELECT p.id AS project_id,
       COALESCE(t.task_count, 0) AS task_count,
       COALESCE(d.dependency_edge_count, 0) AS dependency_edge_count,
       ROUND(COALESCE(h.total_hours, 0), 2) AS total_hours
FROM projects AS p
LEFT JOIN task_totals AS t ON t.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN dependency_totals AS d ON d.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN time_totals AS h ON h.project_id = p.id
ORDER BY project_id;

It does not request data modification and only relies on existing tables (projects, tasks, dependencies, time_entries). It is answerable in this read-only context.

question: Compare treatment and control yield for each experiment using completed runs only. First average non-NULL yield readings within each run, then average those run means within each variant so runs have equal weight. Ignore runs with no known yield and include only experiments with a known mean for both variants. Return experiment_id, control_mean, treatment_mean, and percent_change, in that order. Percent change is 100 times (treatment minus control) divided by control; return NULL when control is zero. Round all three calculated values to two decimals and sort by experiment_id.
reference_sql:
WITH run_means AS
    (SELECT r.id AS run_id,
            r.experiment_id,
            r.variant,
            AVG(x.value) AS mean_yield
     FROM runs AS r
     JOIN measurements AS x ON x.run_id = r.id
     WHERE r.status = 'completed'
         AND x.metric = 'yield'
         AND x.value IS NOT NULL
     GROUP BY r.id,
              r.experiment_id,
              r.variant),
     experiment_means AS
    (SELECT experiment_id,
            AVG(CASE
                    WHEN variant = 'control' THEN mean_yield
                END) AS control_mean,
            AVG(CASE
                    WHEN variant = 'treatment' THEN mean_yield
                END) AS treatment_mean
     FROM run_means
     GROUP BY experiment_id)
SELECT experiment_id,
       ROUND(control_mean, 2) AS control_mean,
       ROUND(treatment_mean, 2) AS treatment_mean,
       ROUND(100.0 * (treatment_mean - control_mean) / NULLIF(control_mean, 0), 2) AS percent_change
FROM experiment_means
WHERE control_mean IS NOT NULL
    AND treatment_mean IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY experiment_id;
